ruleCards.title: Har + supine
ruleCards.rule: The perfect tense is har + the supine form of the verb. It works like English “have done”.
ruleCards.watch: Har is the same for everyone: jag har, du har, vi har, de har.

ruleCards.title: Supine: groups I–III
ruleCards.rule: Group I adds -t to the infinitive. Group II drops the -a and adds -t. Group III adds -tt.
ruleCards.watch: Group II never gets -at: köpt, not köpat.

ruleCards.title: Supine: group IV
ruleCards.rule: Many irregular verbs end in -it in the supine. Some very common ones are fully irregular.
ruleCards.watch: The vowel often changes: dricka → druckit.

ruleCards.title: Irregular supines to learn
ruleCards.rule: These common verbs have their own supine forms. Learn them by heart.
ruleCards.watch: Har haft = have had. Both words are needed.

ruleCards.title: Ever, never, already, not yet
ruleCards.rule: Use the perfect with aldrig (never), någon gång (ever), redan (already) and ännu inte (not yet), when no finished time is mentioned.
examples: Jag har aldrig varit i Lappland.
I have never been to Lapland.
Har du någon gång ätit surströmming?
Have you ever eaten fermented herring?
ruleCards.watch: You can also say: Bussen har inte kommit ännu.

ruleCards.title: I + period: still true
ruleCards.rule: Har + supine + i + a period means something started in the past and is still going on.
examples: Jag har bott här i tio år.
I have lived here for ten years (and still do).
Hon har jobbat på sjukhuset i fem år.
She has worked at the hospital for five years.
Vi har bott i huset sedan 2010.
We have lived in the house since 2010.
ruleCards.watch: English uses “for” here, Swedish uses i: i tio år.

ruleCards.title: Bodde or har bott?
ruleCards.rule: Past tense (bodde) = it’s over. Perfect (har bott) = it’s still true now.
examples: Jag bodde i Sverige i två år.
I lived in Sweden for two years (I don’t now).
Jag har bott i Finland i två år.
I have lived in Finland for two years (I still do).
ruleCards.watch: Ask yourself: do I still live there? Yes → har bott. No → bodde.

ruleCards.title: Finished time → past, no time → perfect
ruleCards.rule: If you say when it happened (igår, förra året, i måndags), use the past. If the time is not said or not finished, use the perfect.
examples: Vi reste till Stockholm förra året.
We travelled to Stockholm last year.
Vi har rest mycket i år.
We have travelled a lot this year.
ruleCards.watch: Never har with igår: Jag såg den igår, not Jag har sett den igår.
